children: Intel (INTC) shares jumped about 5% on Wednesday after a report said South Korea's SK Hynix (SKHY) is exploring options that could involve using part of Intel's planned Ohio semiconductor facility.

The discussions are said to be at an early stage and may include a leasing arrangement under which SK Hynix would manufacture memory chips in the United States. Another scenario under consideration could involve a partnership structure that includes Intel and major cloud computing companies seeking additional memory supply capacity.
The report suggested the potential project would mark SK Hynix's first memory chip production operation in the U.S. if an agreement is reached.

No final decision has been made, and the talks remain exploratory. The report also noted that any proposal involving advanced memory technologies, including high-bandwidth memory and DRAM products, could face regulatory or policy scrutiny in South Korea.

SK Hynix said it is evaluating various options, including expanding its manufacturing footprint, but added that no specific plans have been finalized. Intel has not publicly disclosed details regarding any potential arrangement tied to the Ohio facility.

title: Intel Stock Jumps on Report of Potential SK Hynix Ohio Chip Deal
